title: Oakes Children's Center: its final return lists $842,694 of debts passed to a City address

beats.text: A charity’s final federal return. Everything it had left went to one address: 1380 Howard Street.

visual.kicker: Final federal return · 1 to 31 July 2022 · signed 8 August 2023
visual.text: Distributed to “Community Behavioral Health Services, 1380 Howard St, San Francisco”

beats.text: That’s the Public Health department’s address.
This is a lead, not a finding.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: The charity: Oakes Children’s Center, school-based mental health care for children. It closed in July 2022.

visual.label: Oakes Children’s Center
visual.sub: school-based mental health services for children

beats.text: The City had paid it 9,644,910 dollars, almost all through Public Health.

visual.label: paid by the City, fiscal 2017 to 2023

beats.text: The first lead. Its liquidation schedule lists 35,025 dollars of assets, passed to that City address.

visual.title: Schedule N · final return, July 2022
visual.sub: distributed 31 July 2022 to Community Behavioral Health Services, 1380 Howard St

beats.text: And its debts: 195,474 dollars payable,

visual.title: Schedule N · final return, July 2022
visual.sub: distributed 31 July 2022 to Community Behavioral Health Services, 1380 Howard St

beats.text: and 647,220 in notes and other liabilities.

visual.title: Schedule N · final return, July 2022
visual.sub: distributed 31 July 2022 to Community Behavioral Health Services, 1380 Howard St

beats.text: 842,694 dollars of debts, in all.

visual.label: of debts listed as passed to the City address

beats.text: Were the debts paid? The return answers no.
Either the City took on what Oakes owed, or the form names who took its clients.

a: The City took on what Oakes owed
b: The form names the office that took its clients

beats.text: The return does not say which.

a: The City took on what Oakes owed
b: The form names the office that took its clients

beats.text: The second lead.
The national provider register lists 22 organizational provider numbers at 1380 Howard Street.
Among them, the department’s own, and its government-owned pharmacy.

visual.text: CITY AND COUNTY OF SAN FRANCISCO - DPH · CBHS PHARMACY SERVICES
visual.mark: CITY AND COUNTY OF SAN FRANCISCO - DPH

beats.text: So the recipient named is the department that paid Oakes. Its own books can answer this.

visual.kicker: A question for the City’s own books

beats.text: The third lead.
Its net assets fell from 513,221 dollars in 2019
Minus means it owed more than it had.
Part came from a 337,430 dollar cost settlement loss.
A cost settlement is the year-end reckoning of a contract paid on costs.

visual.label: A cost settlement
visual.sub: the year-end reckoning of a contract paid on costs

beats.text: If it was with Public Health, the City may be among the creditors.

visual.label: A cost settlement
visual.sub: the year-end reckoning of a contract paid on costs

beats.text: The fourth lead. The State’s charity registry holds no closing papers for Oakes.

visual.sub: on the State registry’s list for registration 005425

beats.text: In April 2024 it sent a delinquency notice. In February 2025, an envelope came back.

visual.text: Delinquency notice: “is not in good standing”

beats.text: In November 2025 came only a form letter: cure it by January 2026.
Its status in November 2026: delinquent, past due.
The return says the Attorney General was notified. The registry’s list shows nothing of the kind.
Nothing shows money went missing. Or whether Public Health took on any of the debts.

cards: Whether Public Health took on any of the $842,694
Whether the cost settlement was owed to the City

beats.text: The plain reading: its programmes passed to the County’s behavioural-health system, and no debt moved.

visual.label: A transfer of programmes?
visual.sub: the preparer may have named the system that took its clients

beats.text: Its website said OTTP-SF, a Public Health contractor, would take its clients.

visual.line: “All our current clients and their families will receive continuity of care through Occupational Therapy Training Program-San Francisco [OTTP-SF]”

beats.text: What would settle it? Public Health’s close-out record, and anything the registry received from Oakes.

cards.what: Public Health’s record of what it received when Oakes closed, and the cost settlement
Any notice or papers the Attorney General received from Oakes

beats.text: No regulator has ruled on it. The question is for the Public Health department.
A lead is a question, not an accusation.
